narrative: Material PL1__M9491162 shows smooth high-volume daily demand averaging 4,782 units with a statistically significant declining trend and CV of 21.4%. Lead times are unstable (CV 30.7%), contributing ~90% of total lead-time demand variance, making safety stock the primary lever for service protection. The SAP baseline carried zero safety stock, creating uncontrolled stockout exposure at the 95% service level. The recommended (r,Q) policy with SS=10,906 and OQ=71,590 achieves the 95% target, fits within the 114,632-unit storage cap at 72% utilization, and reduces total annual cost by $1,055 (-21.5%) versus the SAP baseline.
warnings: Declining demand trend detected — recommend re-evaluating EOQ annually as annual demand may decrease
Storage capacity constrains the unconstrained EOQ; order quantity capped to maintain safety_stock + OQ <= max_storage_units
5 outlier demand observations detected and winsorized (e.g., near-zero days likely due to shutdowns)

research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth daily demand with moderate CV and unstable lead times suits a continuous-review (r,Q) model: the reorder point absorbs lead-time uncertainty automatically, while the EOQ-derived order quantity minimizes total ordering and holding cost. The MOQ of 28,149 is comfortably below the EOQ of 71,590, so the MOQ constraint does not bind.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity (114,632 units) lightly constrains the policy: SS(10,906) + OQ(71,590) = 82,496 units = 72% utilization, leaving a 32,136-unit buffer. If safety stock were increased (e.g., for higher service levels), the order quantity would need proportional reduction to stay within capacity.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ(28,149) + SS(10,906) = 39,055 < max_storage(114,632); capacity and MOQ constraints are simultaneously feasible
